label: SYNTHETIC

settings.control_noise: true pixel + N(0, 0.3^2 + (0.15 m f/depth)^2) per axis, no outliers
settings.sensors_unmodelled_errors: switched off: map_xy, relief_sd, focal, principal point, misalignment, datum, outliers

base_moderate.note: flat ground, half-resolution images, 2 grey levels of noise

relief_2m.note: rendered terrain relief of 2 m amplitude that the matcher and the map do not know

yaw_5deg.note: initial yaw error of +/-5 deg (sign drawn per descent) in place of the drawn 2 deg

noise_10gl.note: sensitivity: 10 grey levels of image noise (signal-to-noise 2.6 instead of 13)

fullres.note: full 1456 x 1088 images instead of half resolution

limits: SYNTHETIC. The terrain is feasibility.terrain, a sum of six sinusoids with 3.4-17 m wavelengths and a quasi-periodic lattice, not farmland. Its correlation length sets the matcher's precision and its false-match behaviour; the numbers here do not transfer to real imagery.

Images are rendered at 1/binning of the sensor resolution (default 2: 728 x 544, f = 362.3 px) and point sampled with bilinear interpolation onto the 0.5 m map grid (no anti-alias filter, no blur, no exposure change). Half resolution is coarser than the 0.5 m grid above ~180 m and the white image noise is not averaged by the resampling. The 2-descent full-resolution subset shows the effect is negligible here (rms pixel error 0.016-0.053 px against 0.020-0.048 px at half resolution), but it was not run on the lost-lock descent.

The one descent that lost lock (first-fix draw of descent 2: 9.6 m, 3.0 deg tilt, 2.2 deg yaw, i.e. 2.3-2.7 sigma on three components) locked onto a near-exact lattice repeat of the procedural texture: the template correlation at the lock offset (-8.9, -24.3) m is 0.92 (every location above the 0.5 gate) and the texture autocorrelation peaks at (-9, -25) m with 0.93. Real terrain has its own repeat structure (crop rows, parcels) that is not represented, so the lock-loss rate here (1 of 6 first-fix draws) is a property of this texture and of six draws, not an estimate.

The filter is conservative with the unmodelled map, relief and calibration errors switched off (NEES of the horizontal position about 0.3-0.8 instead of 2, in image and control alike), and its map-error inflation dominates its pixel noise. Position error is therefore nearly insensitive to the matcher's noise: image and control agree to a few percent on locked descents, so position error cannot validate the pixel-noise model; only the direct measurement of match error can.

Pinhole camera with the exact intrinsics the filter assumes: no calibration error (focal, principal point, misalignment), no lens distortion, no map datum or per-landmark map error. The flat-ground runs have no relief error either. The Monte Carlo's default unmodelled errors for these are switched off in image and control alike.
No coarse acquisition: the first fix is an initial error drawn from the filter's own first-fix sigmas (3 m, 1-2 deg). The matcher only works inside its +/-16 m window, so this is a tracking test.
A handful of descents per variant; confidence intervals are wide and the variants share truth with the base run.

Landmarks come from a fixed jittered 40 m grid of map points chosen from the PREDICTED pose, not from pre-selected high-contrast map features. Requiring the whole 48 m search patch inside the image limits the landmarks near 80 m to a few in the middle of the frame.
Match errors within a frame share one pose error and are not independent; the filter treats them as independent.
Host timings come from a PC shared with a running Monte Carlo and throttling; they are not Raspberry Pi timings.

analysis.lost_lock_definition: horizontal error above 10 m at the last frame above 78 m
